summary: One-page cover-letter style template for a standalone AI-generated dietary and supplement recommendation: clinic letterhead and logo, patient lines, a single CP output slot, review lines and a closing block naming a physician. Fixed labels are English, while the language selector and the running header are German, and the audit lists the template as German with German CP output (inferred). The export shows one accounted use (a comparison report run), but standalone CP recommendations bypass accounting, so real use is likely higher.

theme.page: A4 portrait; margins 20 mm left, right and top, 17.5 mm bottom (header 12.5 mm, footer 4 mm); 1 page
theme.cover: letterhead: practice block top left and clinic logo of about 88 x 40 mm top right, anchored behind text
theme.fonts: Calibri (theme minor font) 11 pt body with bold labels; practice name in Tahoma bold; title 12 pt bold; header Calibri 11 pt; footer 9 pt; no Japanese glyphs needed
theme.colours: black text; dark navy for the header and the contact text box; lime green accent; other colour only in the logo
theme.header: from page 2 only: German report title, patient last and first name, German birth-date label and slot, page number
theme.footer: from page 2: contact line (company line), 9 pt; the first-page footer is empty and an anchored text box near the foot of page 1 repeats the contact line

images.detail: a theme texture is stored but not placed

theme_gaps: different first page: empty first-page footer replaced by an anchored contact text box on page 1
running header with patient slots and a page number from page 2
letterhead logo anchored behind text at a fixed position

elements.what: Letterhead block top left: practice name, company form, names of three physicians, street, town, phone and e-mail
elements.note: Contact content; it holds person names, which a clinic block may hold but this analysis does not reproduce. Inside the content control that holds the whole body

elements.what: Clinic logo top right (about 88 x 40 mm, anchored behind text)
Contact line: an anchored text box near the foot of page 1, and the same line in the default footer from page 2
elements.note: One contact content counted once; the duplicate exists because the first-page footer is empty (theme gap: different first page)

elements.what: Header from page 2: report title, patient last and first name, birth-date label and slot, page number; title and label in German in an English template
elements.note: Slots and layout are clinic header content; the German wording is a language defect a translated clinic header fixes. Rarely printed, since the template has one page

elements.what: Bold report title naming the report type (dietary advice derived from the EEG)
elements.note: The core gives no nutrition advice (intended-use section 4)

elements.what: Patient lines: name, birth date, age, report date
elements.note: Patient slots; reportDate is the generation date (audit 14d); pat_age is not described in the audit (unclear)

elements.what: Assessment line with a fixed value naming ADHD
elements.note: Fixed for every patient; in V4 the reason for assessment is clinician text. Could be held as clinic text but must not be

elements.what: Nutrition and supplement recommendation slot filled by CP
elements.note: Standalone CP recommendation (audit 20_cp section 5, standalone row; 12_report_chain section 3): it calls the report generator directly and is not accounted (15_data_schemas C.1), and its output is German whatever the report language (20_cp, inferred). The CP journal shows 18 nutrition runs in August and 7 in September 2026 (16_client_usage section 6); which template they used is not proven

elements.what: Prepared-by line with the clinic name
Medical review line printing one answer of the personal and clinical history form inside questionnaire blocks
elements.note: Later module (table 3.3). The CP anonymiser reads this tag as patient-identifying data (audit 20_cp section 3); which question A11 is, is unclear
Filled per report by the clinician

elements.what: Closing block: clinic name, a product line, the company name, a named physician and a professional title
elements.note: Rule 14: fixed named signatory typed into the template

elements.what: Language selector set to German in a template with English labels
elements.note: Control marker (rule 2); the template has a language selector only, no patient-information line

not_expressible.what: Fixed named physician in the closing block
not_expressible.why: A report is final when the issuing clinician issues it (spec 3.5); a typed signatory signs every report
not_expressible.suggestion: An issue-time signature block filled from the issuing user (name, qualification, date and time of issue, report version)

review_response.finding: F7 (pseudonymisation): exact report counts and shares equal the export manifest and allow re-identification
review_response.reason: reports_per_year and share_pct are taken from usage_rounded.json (rounded).

review_response.finding: F31 (classify-2): the extractor skipped content controls; re-extract and re-check every model
review_response.reason: Model rebuilt from tpl_extract_v2 (content controls, text boxes, headers and footers) and checked against the raw XML of the docx.

review_response.finding: F98 (completeness): one class rule per feature, a separate leave-out class, and every element needing a listed schema change classed not_expressible
review_response.reason: Brief v2 rules applied: leave_out with leave_reason replaces dropped or not_expressible for control lines and similar content; every element behind a not_expressible list entry has that class and its gap code.

review_response.finding: F79 (numbers): the same legacy feature gets different classes depending on the modelling group
review_response.reason: Same rule set as all groups: table of contents TG5, hidden control and language lines leave_out control_marker, no manual checklist tables in this template set.

review_response.finding: F2 and F3 (pseudonymisation): close paraphrases of fixed sentences and an overstated no-quote claim
review_response.reason: Descriptions state the function of a text, not its wording. Checked: no run of 4 words (hyphens split) of the raw docx text, including content controls, text boxes, headers and footers, occurs in this file apart from marker names; no Japanese characters occur in it.

review_response.finding: F105 (completeness): suggestions that cross hard rule 5 (draft starters, condition or treatment rows)
review_response.reason: No suggestion in this model proposes a feature whose use is treatment advice, diagnosis or a prefilled verdict.

review_response.finding: F108 and F81 (completeness, numbers): claim wording was counted only on clinic-class elements and the per-model field disagreed with the report
review_response.reason: claim_wording and claim_kind are set on every element whatever its class; the old field claim_wording_clinic_blocks is dropped.

review_response.finding: F42 (classify-2, rule for all): footnotes are not modelled and are not a block kind
review_response.reason: Checked in the raw XML: this template has no footnote references, so no footnote element is needed.

review_response.finding: F1, F57 and F78 (pseudonymisation, classify-4, numbers): e05 reproduced the printed report title
review_response.reason: e05 now describes the function only; quote check run against all XML text of the raw docx with hyphens split.

review_response.finding: F4 (pseudonymisation): T15 belongs to the same clinic as T10 and T11
review_response.reason: clinic is Clinic F, per pseudonym_map.json.

review_response.finding: F6 (pseudonymisation): exact brand hex colours recorded
review_response.reason: Colours are plain names only.

review_response.finding: F66 (classify-4): the language selector was not_expressible, giving 91% coverage
review_response.reason: e13 is leave_out control_marker (rule 2); the language mismatch is noted in e04, e13 and the summary.

review_response.finding: F67 (classify-4): standalone CP recommendations are not accounted, so 1 report a year undercounts; the e08 note was wrong
review_response.reason: Export figure kept; summary and e08 cite the audit (12_report_chain, 15_data_schemas C.1, 20_cp section 5, 16_client_usage section 6).

review_response.finding: F76 (classify-4): the A11 answer tag is a patient-identifying tag for the CP anonymiser; the audit lists the template as German
review_response.reason: e10 note cites 20_cp section 3; summary says the audit lists the template as German and e08 notes German CP output (inferred). language stays EN for the fixed labels.

review_response.finding: F89 (numbers): mixed language in T15; T15 has a language selector only
review_response.reason: e04 and e13 notes record the German header and selector; no patient-information line exists.

review_response.finding: F90 (numbers): the contact line duplicated as a text box is in no list
review_response.reason: Recorded as theme gap (different first page) and in the e03 note; it needs no schema change beyond the theme, so it is not a not_expressible element.

review_response.finding: F103 (completeness): signature blocks counted as covered clinic content
review_response.reason: e12 is not_expressible TG11.

review_response.finding: F97 (completeness): content controls hid the whole body of T15
review_response.reason: Re-checked against tpl_extract_v2: every body paragraph sits in a content control and all are modelled; the header is modelled as e04.

review_response.finding: Review 2026-10-29 A5: questionnaires are a later module in table 3.3 of the shared document of 29 October, no longer an open question
review_response.reason: Every element of the questionnaire row, with the cognitive tests and the questionnaire-derived fields that follow it, is reclassified from open to later_module; counts updated.

review_response.finding: Review 2026-10-29 C11: coverage gap ids G1 to G12 clash with the open question ids of the specification repository
review_response.reason: Coverage gaps renamed TG1 to TG12 in every field of this model.
